subject: physics

items.q: Why do the planets stay in orbit around the Sun?
items.correct: Gravity provides a centripetal force that pulls them towards the Sun, curving their path into an orbit.
items.misconception: There is no force on a planet in orbit, which is why it keeps moving.
items.random_wrong: The Sun pushes them round with solar wind.
items.why: An orbit needs a centripetal force; gravity constantly changes the planet's direction. Without it the planet would fly off in a straight line.

items.q: What does the red-shift of distant galaxies tell us?
items.correct: They are moving away from us — the universe is expanding.
items.misconception: The galaxies are red-hot, which is why their light looks red.
items.why: Red-shift stretches wavelengths as a source recedes. It is key evidence that the universe is expanding, supporting the Big Bang.

items.correct: A distance — how far light travels in one year.
items.misconception: A length of time — how long light has existed.
items.random_wrong: The time light takes to reach Earth from the Sun.
items.why: Despite the word 'year', a light-year measures distance (~9.5 × 10¹⁵ m), used because distances in space are so huge.
